overview.eyebrow: For councils, tourist offices and local businesses
overview.title: Your region’s places and events on one map — no app.
overview.lead: Visitors open it on their phone, filter, and go. You share one link.
overview.introP1: HelloLocal is a browser-based local tourism map. It brings a region’s sights, services, hospitality, special places and events onto one screen. No app to install, no account to browse, no hopping between websites.
overview.introP2: A region is more than its famous landmarks. Family cellars, craft workshops, tucked-away restaurants and local producers deserve a shared, easy-to-share presence. Place owners write their own pages; the council or tourist office passes everything on with a single link.
overview.differenceKicker: Why it is not just another map
overview.differenceTitle: Not the world atlas — your region
overview.differenceLead: Google Maps shows everything. HelloLocal highlights what matters locally: curated places, up-to-date events, texts written by the people who run them, and one shareable link.
overview.seoTitle: HelloLocal | Local places and events on a regional map
overview.seoDescription: A browser tourism map for councils, tourist offices and local businesses. Places, events, multiple languages — no app, one link.
overview.keywords: local tourism, regional map, municipality, tourist office, local business, craft, HelloLocal
overview.shotCaption: Szeged on the map: places, filters and upcoming events on one screen.
overview.statsApp: guests open it in the browser
overview.featuresLead: Map and list, opening hours, what’s on today, several languages — with content that stays in local hands.

hidden.title: What only locals used to know
hidden.text: Courtyards, workshops, market stalls, cellars, one turn off the main street. They go on the map so guests can find them — instead of disappearing in a global atlas.

traffic.title: One link for official and tourism channels
traffic.text: Website, newsletter, QR code, poster. A coherent presence from a modest marketing budget — without building an ad machine.

region.title: Country → region → town → place
region.text: Several settlements can share one system, each with its own audience. Smaller towns do not have to build a full tourism site alone.

overview.storiesLead: Guests explore. Businesses maintain their own pages. Councils and tourist offices present the whole offer with one link.
overview.closingTitle: Show your region on one map.
overview.closingText: Open the live example and picture your own places on those pins: the workshop, the cellar, the service, or the whole area.
overview.closingImageAlt: A hiker with a yellow backpack on a mountain trail

collect.title: Places go on the map
collect.text: Sights, hospitality, services, makers. Photos, opening hours, and a page guests can forward.

publish.title: Events stay current
publish.text: The coming weeks sit beside the map. What has ended drops off; what’s on this weekend stays in front.

share.title: One link for the guest
share.text: Optionally on your own domain (for example helloetyek.hu), in the guest’s language. Works in the phone browser — no new app.

app.q: Does a guest have to download an app?
app.a: No. The map and events open in the browser, on phone and desktop. Sign-in is only needed to leave a rating.

languages.a: Hungarian, English and German. Content is managed per language — not a blunt machine translation. Search can find each language on its own address.

editors.a: Whoever runs the place: the business, the service, or staff at the council or tourist office. Everyone looks after their own part. An AI helper can draft copy; traffic is shown in aggregate — visitor personal data is not sold.

towns.q: Can several settlements share one system?
towns.a: Yes. Countries hold regions; regions hold towns. Each keeps its own character; the guest stays with the place they opened.

maps.a: Google Maps shows the whole world. HelloLocal shows your region: curated local offer, up-to-date events, pages written by place owners, optional own domain, and one shareable link for tourism communication. It is not an advertising marketplace, and you do not push a new app onto guests.

places.title: Places with their own page
places.text: Opening hours, photos, introduction. Lesser-known spots show up too — not only what sits on the main square.

events.title: Events that stay in front
events.text: What has ended comes off. What’s on now is what guests see first — including a spontaneous weekend.

map.title: A map you can set off from
map.text: Filters for what’s open, what’s good in the rain, what’s on today. Mobile-friendly, no registration to browse.

languages.title: Three languages, real content
languages.text: Businesses can tailor each language to its audience. Language versions can have their own web addresses.

sites.title: Your own domain for the region
sites.text: hellolocal.hu presents the product. A region domain — for example helloetyek.hu — opens straight onto that area’s map.

editors.title: Content stays local
editors.text: No central newsroom writing for you. AI can help with wording; you get aggregate traffic figures — we don’t sell personal data.

maker.title: The workshop gets its own page
maker.text: Ceramics, textiles, jam, a cellar. Photos, hours, events — guests see what you keep up to date.
maker.alt: Handmade ceramic bowls on a workshop table

service.title: Your name comes first
service.text: Hospitality, lodging, local services. Guests look at the area and find your address — not a distant generic list.
service.alt: A small bicycle workshop with tools and a wheel on the bench

quiet.title: One corner further still matters
quiet.text: Courtyards, market stalls, heritage spots. Places only locals knew go on the map too.
quiet.alt: An open courtyard gate on a quiet side street

town.title: One surface, one link
town.text: Gather the offer of your towns and surroundings. Embed it on the website, use it in campaigns — including thematic curator pages.
town.alt: A live map of local places and events
